item.title: Could Your Anterior Leg Pain Be Caused by Lumbar Nerve Issues?
item.description:
The post Could Your Anterior Leg Pain Be Caused by Lumbar Nerve Issues? appeared first on iRunFar.

Last month, we outlined the concept of neurogenic hip, thigh, and knee pain, and how nerve pain, especially from the upper to mid-lumbar spine, can cause and perpetuate common running-related pains in these areas.

Common running complaints — hip impingement, IT band syndrome, patellofemoral pain — can all be either amplified or outright caused by irritated nerves from the L1 to L4 lumbar segments.

The solution to these stubborn, often chronic issues isn’t treatment of the hip, thigh, or knee. Instead, the key to a successful resolution is a treatment plan that examines and treats nerve irritation in the lumbar spine.

item.title: Jane Maus Sets Women’s FKT on Colorado’s First Flatiron
item.description:
The post Jane Maus Sets Women’s FKT on Colorado’s First Flatiron appeared first on iRunFar.

On November 5, 2026, Jane Maus set a new women’s fastest known time on the First Flatiron, a short but technical climbing and running route in Boulder, Colorado. Completing the route in 37:07, she bettered the previous women’s record, set by Bailee Mulholland, of 41:06 by nearly four minutes.

The Flatirons are a series of iconic, steeply tilted sandstone slabs located on the eastern slope of Green Mountain. Five major Flatirons, numbered First through Fifth from north to south, make up the main group.
